title.narrative: FAO resilience, food security and social cohesion in Burkina Faso 2023-2025
FAO resiliensprojekt för matsäkerhet och social sammanhållning i BF 2023-2025

description.narrative: Insatsen syftar till att stärka resiliensen/motståndskraften hos utsatta pastoralister och agro-pastoralister mot flerdimensionella kriser, att förbättra deras livsmedelsförsörjning och att minska undernäring samt stärka kvinnors och ungdomars socioekonomiska egenmakt, samtidigt som fredliga och inkluderande samhällen uppmuntras.

The objectives of the contribution are to: (i) improve the resilience to multidimensional shocks/crises and the food and nutritional security of targeted vulnerable pastoral and agro-pastoral households; (ii) increase the socio-economic empowerment of women and young people; and, (iii) encourage peaceful and inclusive societies.
The project is implemented in the four regions Sahel, Nord, Centre-Nord and Boucle du Mouhoun in Burkina Faso.

The overall objective of the programme is to strengthen the resilience to multidimensional chocks/crises, increase the food and nutritional security of targeted vulnerable pastoral and agro-pastoral households, as well as to increase the socio-economic empowerment of women and young people, for peaceful and inclusive societies in the Sahel, Northern, Centre-North and Boucle du Mouhoun regions of Burkina Faso.
Concretely, this means that number of food insecure households are reduced, that households Resilience Capacity Index (RCI) and growth rate of average household income is increased in the project area.
The objectives/outcomes resulting from the project's action are based on the three pillars of the Caisse de Résilience approach (technical, social and financial support) and the triple Humanitarian-Development-Peace (HDP) Nexus approach.
The project is designed around four reinforced specific objectives/outcomes as follows:
Outcome 1: The livelihoods of targeted households are strengthened through the adoption of innovative techniques and technologies to increase their production and productivity;
Outcome 2: Identified profitable agro-silvo-pastoral value chains are professionalized and generate income and decent jobs in targeted regions;
Outcome 3: Local governance and social cohesion around peaceful and sustainable access and management of shared natural resources is strengthened.
Outcome 4: The incidence of malnutrition among targeted vulnerable households is reduced.

The results presented are documented in the Final report and project highlights (Dox 24/001040-32) Key results:
Under Outcome 1 (Strengthening the target households livelihoods by adopting innovative techniques and technologies):
- Delivered training and awareness-raising sessions on integrating conflict prevention and management. Assessments and tools were shared with the participants and several consultations and dialogues were held.
- 482 people (the target was 400) were made aware of the regional and national texts governing natural resource use and management, pastoralism and transhumance.
- An overview of pastoral resources was prepared to promote the establishment of a feed balance for the agropastoral season.
- 48 agropastoral field schools (APFSs) were set up to promote climate-smart agricultural techniques, with the involvement of 816 members (including 326 women) throughout the project's intervention area.
- Two market garden production sites, each comprising one hectare, were also equipped with a solar pump system to ensure rational water use and to lessen the drudgery of the beneficiaries' work.
- More than 400 households received support in agricultural inputs (vegetable seeds and fertilizers), enabling the development of approximately 4 ha of land.
- 36 livestock-breeding staff (including six women) were trained in epizootics control and prevention.
Under Outcome 2 (Professionalization of the identified profitable agrosylvopastoral value chains):
- Provided support to breeding units in the Sahel region by supplying 5 000 tonnes of livestock feed,
- Support for the revitalization of 12 microenterprises by training 23 (23 participants of 24 expected) of their members in business management.
- 22 village savings and loan associations (VSLAs) were set up, with a total of 550 members (including 385 women) (70 percent).
- 27 internal training instructors continued as part of the cascade training effort in agricultural entrepreneurship, with 439 beneficiaries trained (compared with a target of 400), including 223 women.
Under Outcome 3 (Enhancing local governance and social cohesion around access to and the peaceful and sustainable management of shared natural resources):
- 11 transhumance (seasonal migration) committees were supported (against a target of eight). With the aim of revitalizing the consultation workshops, four fora were organized in four sessions.
- 57 Dimitra clubs were set up and facilitated, with a total of 1 334 members (including 638 women). (A Dimitra club is a group of women, men and young people who organize on a voluntary basis to bring about changes in their communities and resolve problems using their own resources, without relying on external support). FAO thinks it is likely that the clubs will continue after the end of the project Given the enthusiasm shown, the effective involvement of stakeholders and the maturity of the platforms
Under Outcome 4 (Reducing the incidence of malnutrition in target households):
- Raising awareness among identified beneficiaries, and providing them with training opportunities in, good infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices. Two awareness-raising/training sessions were organized for mothers who are to receive nutrition support on good IYCF practices
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
